column2: req_desc

Sign-in and sign-out
A seeded member who signs in with a wrong password sees the sign-in refusal, then signs in with the published password, lands on the published landing route (their role's home screen, or the allowed `next` screen) and signs out back to Sign in.

Same answer for every address
Sign-in failures, password-reset requests and invitations answer with the same status and body whether or not the email address belongs to a member, as qualified in API.

Invitations and password reset
The launch producer invites a teammate by email, the invitee sets a password from the emailed link and lands signed in on their role's home screen, and any member can reset a forgotten password from an emailed link.

Member records stay in their workspace
A member id from another brand's workspace answers 404 with the same body as an unknown id on every member endpoint.

Only the launch producer manages members
Inviting, changing a role and removing a member succeed only for the launch producer and answer 403 for every other role, except that a stockist buyer, who can see no other member, gets 404 for another member's id.

Public drop calendar
A shopper browses public drops grouped by Copenhagen ISO week with status marks, filters, search, sort and paging, and on a 375x812 phone opens the filters as a bottom sheet with a sticky result-count bar.

Calendar state lives in the URL
Market, status, type, week, search, sort and page are read from and written to the address, each change adds exactly one history entry, and Back and Forward restore each step.

Status never by colour alone
Drop statuses show their word plus a distinct mark and Night pins show a moon mark plus the word Night, with text contrast at WCAG 2.2 AA.

Withdrawn drops are gone
A withdrawn drop's page answers 410 with the withdrawn page and the drop is absent from the calendar, search, the public drops API and the sitemap.

Copenhagen calendar dates
Today, ISO weeks and week labels on the public calendar follow the Copenhagen calendar whatever the browser's time zone.

Joining a waitlist on a phone
On a 375x812 phone a shopper fills the waitlist form above a sticky Join bar that never covers the focused field, confirms from the emailed link and sees their place confirmed.

One join and one reply
A waitlist join answers identically for known and unknown addresses, and a double submit records one join and sends one opt-in email.

Opt-in links work once
An opt-in link confirms the member once, then answers as used, and answers as expired from OPT_IN_LINK_TTL_SECONDS after issue.

Waitlist rate limit
The sixth waitlist join from one client address within WAITLIST_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS answers 429 with Retry-After in whole seconds, keyed on the first X-Forwarded-For entry.

Waitlist names
Line breaks in a shopper's name never add mail headers or change a subject, and the name limit counts user-perceived characters.

Planning a drop on the embargo dial
The launch producer sets a drop's date, type and time on the embargo dial by pointer, by keyboard alone and by touch at 375x812, saves the time and schedules the drop, with every planner date on the Copenhagen calendar whatever the browser's zone.

Dial slider keys and spoken value
The dial's slider steps by the published keys without wrapping and speaks the exact Copenhagen time of the drop.

Market pins, local times and Night
On every dial change the six pins show each market's local time and Night state in their text and data attributes, and the dial root shows the UTC instant that Save time will store.

Simultaneous go-live rules
A simultaneous drop accepts a whole-second UTC instant or a Copenhagen local time, refuses a spring-forward gap time and a time not later than now, and maps a repeated autumn time to its first occurrence.

Rolling go-live per market
A rolling drop opens at the same local time in each market's own zone, shifts a market's gap time forward by the gap's length and returns each market's instant.

Weekly restock series
A weekly restock series keeps its Copenhagen wall-clock time, lists its next 8 UTC instants and adds its pieces at each instant exactly once.

New-drop draft survives reload
The multi-step New drop form restores its step and every typed value after a reload until the drop is created.

Dial motion and reduced motion
The dial hand and pins turn over 280 milliseconds, changed countdown digits roll over 140 milliseconds, Night marks fade in over 140 milliseconds and the markets sheet rises over 560 milliseconds, and with reduced motion each changes at once with identical values.

Go-live offers holds
Within 10 seconds after a market's go-live instant the drop is live there and that market's confirmed waitlist members, in join order and while store pieces last, each get one hold and one hold email.

Hold expiry passes the piece on
A claim at or after a hold's expiry instant is refused, and within 10 seconds the piece is offered to the next confirmed member in join order exactly once, while the hold page counts the hold down by the server's clock, within 2 seconds, even when the device clock is hours off.

Claim idempotency
A claim replayed with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the original response, and the same key with a different body answers 409.

One winner for the last piece
When several shoppers claim a market's last open piece at once exactly one succeeds and the others get the lost-race refusal with the winning time in Copenhagen time.

Pieces left stay exact
Pieces left on the drop page and in the public API always equal the market's store pieces minus claims minus live holds, across every running app copy.

Claiming a held piece on a phone
On a 375x812 phone a shopper opens the emailed hold link, watches the hold countdown roll only its changed digits and claims the piece from the sticky Claim bar.

Requesting and splitting an edition
Stockist buyers request quantities per style and the merchandiser splits the edition by keyboard in the Split edition dialog and sees each stockist's share.

Largest-remainder split
Each stockist gets its proportional share rounded down, leftover pieces go one each by largest fractional remainder with ties to the earliest request, and an oversubscribed style's shares sum to its wholesale edition.

Stockist buyers see only their store
A stockist buyer gets only the published buyer fields for their own store, and any other store's stockist, allocation or invoice answers 404.

Versioned allocation edits
An allocation save carries the version it was read at, a stale save answers 412 naming who saved and when, and the screen rolls back to the saved values and announces it.

Confirming an allocation
The finance lead reviews the quote and confirms an allocation by keyboard in the Confirm allocation dialog and sees its invoice number and priced lines.

Price list in force
Confirmation prices each line from the price list in force on the Copenhagen date of confirmation, and allocations confirmed earlier keep their prices on the allocation page, the invoice, the allocation line sheet and the email.

Exact money and Danish VAT
Amounts are integer minor units in the stockist's currency with yen in whole yen, and Copenhagen stockists get 25% VAT on each line rounded half up on its own.

Confirmation is all or nothing
Confirming records the confirmed allocation, one Kill Bill invoice with one item per line and one confirmation email together, and with Kill Bill down answers 503 with nothing recorded or mailed.

Confirm once
A double-clicked Confirm or two simultaneous confirm requests produce exactly one confirmation, one invoice and one email.

Line-sheet export
A drop's line sheet exports as CSV with the published columns, prices from the list in force and formula-like cells neutralised.

Legacy line-sheet import
Importing the previous tool's semicolon line sheet matches style numbers ignoring case and surrounding spaces, merges duplicates with the later row winning, reports orphan line numbers and changes nothing on re-import.

Import limits and methods
The import answers 413 above 1,000,000 file bytes, 415 for a wrong content type and 405 with an Allow header for a wrong method.

Importing a line sheet
The merchandiser imports a line sheet by keyboard in the Import line sheet dialog and reads the import report, whose first column stays pinned at 375x812 with no page overflow.

Safe look uploads
Look images are judged by decoded content, stored with location data removed and orientation applied, limited by the published file and alt-text limits, and refused with nothing stored while MinIO is down.

Look reorder
Looks reorder by drag or by keyboard with each move announced, the order persists, and a stale reorder answers 412 and the list rolls back to the saved order.

Looks on a phone
On a 375x812 phone a shopper swipes a drop's look carousel with an n / total counter and a merchandiser reorders looks by touch.

Preview link lifecycle
A preview link expires PREVIEW_LINK_TTL_SECONDS after issue, dies when revoked or regenerated, and refuses any write, and an open press page switches to the matching dead-link screen within 10 seconds of its link dying.

Press surfaces carry only press fields
The press page, its API and the press email carry exactly the published press fields and never wholesale prices, stockist names, internal notes or staff emails.

Press ZIP and manifest
The press ZIP holds each look image with location data removed plus a manifest of each file's name, size in bytes and SHA-256, and answers 503 while MinIO is down.

Reading a preview on a phone
On a 375x812 phone a press editor reads the preview and downloads the images from a sticky Download bar, and a dead link shows its matching dead-link copy.

Story allowlist
Drop stories keep only the published elements and http, https and mailto links on save, and the public drop page renders only those.

Versioned story saves
A story save carries the version it was read at, and a stale save answers 412 naming who saved and when while the typed text stays in the editor.

Story announcements
Each story save, publish, stale refusal, ended session and outage is announced with its exact copy in the Story status live region.

Writing and publishing a story
The press lead writes and publishes a story by keyboard, and after a session ends mid-edit signs in again to find the draft restored.

Danish order with stable pages
The stockist directory lists stockists in Danish alphabetical order with cursor pages capped at 50 that never repeat or skip a stockist while others are added or archived.

Archive and exact restore
An archived stockist answers 404 and leaves lists, search and the CSV export, and restoring brings it back exactly with its allocations.

Contact erasure
Erasing a stockist's contact removes its name, email and phone from the directory, exports and queued email while invoice amounts stay under the published placeholder.

Managing the directory
The merchandiser adds, archives, restores and erases by keyboard through the directory dialogs, and at 375x812 the directory shows as cards above a sticky bar.

Start-up, health and several copies
The app starts from run.json, answers health, and several copies started together against one database run every start-up step safely and every scheduled effect and email exactly once.

One error ladder and published surface
Every API path follows the published error-precedence ladder, and answers 404 outside the API table, 405 with Allow for a wrong method and 415 for a wrong content type.

Ended sessions and removed access
A session ends SESSION_TTL_SECONDS after sign-in, the next request answers the session-ended 401, the screen keeps its draft and restores it after signing in again, and removed access refuses the next action with its copy.

Forms and dialogs report problems
Every form shows field errors inline and in a Problems summary whose links move focus to their fields, and a refused dialog stays open with everything typed and focus on its error.

Published formats
Every value uses the published formats: whole-second UTC instants and integer minor units in the API, and market times, money, ISO weeks and position counters as published on screen and in email.

Viewports and accessibility audit
Every screen fits 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal overflow or covered control and passes an automated WCAG 2.2 AA audit with its dialogs and sheets open, and each screen that publishes a phone or tablet layout switches between its phone, tablet and desktop layouts at exactly 768 and 1024 pixels wide.

Motion system
All motion uses exactly 140, 280 and 560 milliseconds as style-sheet transitions, style-sheet animations or element animations with reduced-motion substitutes, pointer effects follow each event's pointer type, and the intro roll, route wipe, card glide, swatch dots and header tone flip behave as published.

Stone-and-night look
Screens read as hairline-ruled panels on a warm stone ground with near-black night sections, a single vermilion accent and mono numerals on a shared baseline, as described in Visual design.

Embargo dial craft
The embargo dial reads at a glance as a 24-hour ring with a dark night arc, concentric market pins with printed local times and a ruled six-market ledger beside it.

Provider wiring from configuration
Every provider URL and credential is read from the environment at start, never hard-coded or sent to the browser, and every recorded effect goes to the real provider.
/app/run.json exists with exactly the string fields _schema (run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font and icon set, each with its licence.
Every shipped package and bundled asset is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1.
The app stores data only in the provided Postgres database and MinIO bucket; no other database server, embedded database file or cache service appears in its dependencies or code.
Fonts, icons, styles and scripts are served from /app itself; no page loads anything from another origin.
Look images and illustrations in the app are generated by its own code; /app contains no photographs or copied image files.
/app/package-lock.json is committed and the install command installs from it.
